IR.rationale: Trend followers have tended to hold long bond-futures exposure, so falling intermediate yields relative to policy rates mark a bond rally that feeds directly into CTA returns.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads signal the onset of risk-off regimes. Such regimes tend to produce persistent cross-asset trends that trend followers exploit, the 'crisis alpha' pattern.

V.rationale: Elevated equity volatility marks the extreme-market states in which trend-following payoffs resemble a long lookback straddle (Fung and Hsieh).

AP.rationale: Equity selloffs are when trend followers have historically earned positive returns as short positions build. This is the convex, crisis-alpha side of the return smile.

ST.rationale: Cross-sectional momentum profits co-move with time-series momentum. A strong momentum factor indicates a trending, non-reverting market environment.

FX.rationale: Broad dollar moves are among the most persistent macro trends. Dollar strength episodes are a recurring source of CTA currency profits.

COM.rationale: Sustained commodity declines are captured by trend followers through short futures positions and positive roll in contango. The state of broad commodity returns therefore indexes a key CTA profit channel.

MC.rationale: Financial stress regimes coincide with deleveraging and directional macro moves that trend strategies monetise.

ENDG.rationale: Trend-following returns show positive autocorrelation because the underlying trends persist across weeks.

IR.rationale: Sharp rises in intermediate yields hit the typical long-bond position of trend followers and trigger rapid position flips. Both raise realised volatility.

B.rationale: Credit spread widening signals a regime shift in risk appetite that increases cross-asset volatility beyond what recent CTA variance captures.

V.rationale: CTA portfolios are diversified across asset classes, so their volatility rises most when implied volatility is high in both equities and safe-haven/metal markets at once.

AP.rationale: Equity declines carry a leverage and volatility-feedback effect that spreads to futures markets and raises next-period variance.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes reflect abrupt trend reversals. These are precisely the episodes when trend-following positions are whipsawed and volatility jumps.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation signals safe-haven flows and carry unwinds, which generate large, correlated FX moves.

COM.rationale: Commodity selloffs tend to come with spiking commodity volatility, raising the variance of the commodity sleeve of CTA books.

MC.rationale: High financial stress predicts elevated future realised volatility across markets beyond the persistence already in own variance.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, so high recent variance relative to its history signals a high-volatility regime. Mean reversion may also temper this effect, and the model can learn the net effect.

IR.rationale: Abrupt yield spikes reverse the long-bond trend that CTAs commonly hold, a classic source of sharp trend-follower drawdowns.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield rallies often mark risk-on reversals after stress, catching trend followers positioned short risk.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the distribution of CTA returns and raises the probability of extreme outcomes on both tails, including losses.

AP.rationale: Sharp equity rebounds are when trend-following short positions are squeezed, mirroring the momentum-crash mechanism.

ST.rationale: Weak momentum together with strong short-term reversal profits describes a mean-reverting, choppy market. That is the environment in which trend strategies suffer their worst losses.

FX.rationale: Sudden yen strength reflects carry unwinds that reverse established FX trends and inflict losses on trend positions.

COM.rationale: Abrupt commodity selloffs can reverse long commodity trends and coincide with broad deleveraging that hurts CTA books.

MC.rationale: Stress regimes raise the dispersion of CTA outcomes, so tail losses become more likely even if the mean is positive.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent CTA returns indicate a trendless or reversing environment, and drawdowns in trend strategies tend to cluster.

IR.rationale: Strong declines in yields signal flight-to-quality bond rallies, the largest single source of outsized trend-follower gains.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads mark the onset of crisis regimes in which persistent directional moves deliver CTA crisis alpha.

V.rationale: Extreme-volatility states are where the straddle-like payoff of trend following produces its largest gains.

AP.rationale: Equity market declines are associated with large positive trend-following returns, the convex left side of the return smile.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum factor returns indicate trending markets, raising the chance of exceptionally strong trend-following performance.

FX.rationale: Powerful dollar rallies are persistent macro trends that have generated outsized CTA currency gains.

COM.rationale: Persistent commodity collapses are monetised by trend followers through short positions and can produce extreme gains.

MC.rationale: Financial stress coincides with the deleveraging episodes in which trend followers have recorded their best periods.

ENDG.rationale: Positive autocorrelation of trend returns means strong recent performance raises the probability of a further large gain.
